title: Creating a screening set of potential anthelmintic compounds using ChEMBL
protocol: Use BLASTP to search all predicted nematode/platyhelminth proteins against the sequences of single-protein targets from the ChEMBL database.
Take the top BLASTP hit with an E-value ≤ 1e-10 for each putative nematode/platyhelminth gene.
Assign a BLAST score of 1 to nematode/platyhelminth genes with high sequence similarity hits to ChEMBL (E ≤ e-85, and ≥80% of the residues in the ChEMBL protein covered by the BLAST match).
Set the BLAST score to zero for genes that do not meet the criteria.
Assign a ChEMBL non-human score of 1 to nematode/platyhelminth proteins matching only non-human targets within ChEMBL.
Search human proteins in the in-house Compara database against ChEMBL 21 proteins using BLASTP.
Set the ChEMBL non-human score to zero for helminth genes where the top ChEMBL BLAST hit matches a human protein (E ≤ 0.05) or belongs to a Compara family containing a human member.
Set a chokepoint score of 1 for nematode/platyhelminth genes predicted to encode chokepoint enzymes and belonging to Compara families with ≥3 predicted chokepoints.
Assign a chokepoint score of 0.1 for predicted chokepoints not belonging to Compara families with ≥3 chokepoints.
Assign a zero score to non-chokepoint enzymes.
Set the multi-species score to zero for nematode/platyhelminth genes in Compara families with only one species.
Set the multi-species score to 1 for nematode/platyhelminth genes not belonging to single-species Compara families.
Calculate a species-distribution score for potential nematode/platyhelminth targets.
Assign a score of 1 if a nematode/platyhelminth gene is present in a Compara family containing ≥90% of the species from a major group of helminths.
Assign a score of 0 otherwise.
Calculate an invertebrate biology score for ChEMBL BLAST hits.
Assign a score of 1 if the top ChEMBL BLAST hit of a nematode/platyhelminth gene is to a UniProt protein from a non-chordate metazoan.
Assign a score of 0 otherwise.
Calculate a singleton score for each gene.
Set the score to 1 for nematode/platyhelminth genes that lack within-species paralogues according to the Compara database.
Assign a zero score to genes with within-species paralogues.
List compounds tagged with MeSH categories 'anthelmintic', ‘anticestodal’, or ‘antinematodal’ in PubChem.
Find compounds listed as having ‘anthelmintic’, ‘anticestodal’, ‘antischistosomal’, ‘antitrematodal’, or ‘fasciolicide’ activity in KEGG Drugs.
Find compounds listed as ‘anthelmintic’ in the ChEBI database.
Find compounds listed in ChEMBL with the keywords ‘anthelmintic’ OR ‘anthelminthic’ in ATC code description, mechanism of action, USAN stem definition, or indication class fields.
Find compounds tagged with MeSH categories 'anthelmintics’, ‘antinematodal’, ‘filaricides’, ‘antiplatyhelmintic’, or ‘schistosomicides’ in DrugBank.
Identify additional compounds by text searching for ‘anthelmintic OR antihelminthic OR antinematodal OR antitrematodal’ in DrugBank.

Find compounds from PubChem identified by searching for ‘anthelmintics OR anthelmintic OR nematocide OR nematicide’, ensuring low structural similarity to previously listed compounds using the Tanimoto coefficient of ECPF4 fingerprints as implemented in RDKit.
Calculate pairwise similarity between SMILES strings of known anthelmintic compounds using ECFP4 fingerprints in RDKit 2016.09.4.
Convert Tanimoto similarities to distances by calculating 1.0 - similarity.
Read the distance matrix into R and perform hierarchical clustering using Ward's minimum variance method.
Cut the dendrogram at a height that separates known chemical classes of anthelmintic compounds.
Further split clusters if their members have little in common regarding chemical structure.
Classify top drug candidates from Step F into chemical classes based on the diversity analysis.
Filter the list of compounds using information on compound-target pairs.
Discard medicinal chemistry compounds that do not co-appear in a PDBe structure with the ChEMBL target or have a median pCHEMBL score of >7.
Use chemical classes identified for further filtering.
Further filter the list by taking compounds listed as available for purchase in ZINC.
For each nematode/platyhelminth target, take the highest-scoring compound from each chemical class according to the compound score.
